questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Den irske kultur har altid virket særlig dragende på mig, og så skader det heller ikke at Trinity College Dublin er et verdensanerkendt universitet med en masse muligheder både på den faglige front og den studenter-sociale.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Super easy. My coordinator at Trinity was super helpful and almost always responded immediatly if there was something I needed to have clarified. The webportal as a new incoming student was also easy to navigate and I got sent notifications each time there was something I was to be aware of.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation week before classes officially started that served as a perfect introduction to everything I would need to know during my stay, and they set up an anonymous option where people could send in all sorts of questions that they would then answer on the spot, which I thought was a really good idea.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got lucky and found housing on my first try, where I shared a house with 4 other students, although I did live about an hour away from campus in bus (I missed the sign-up for the more typical student housing arrangements such as Kavanaugh Court as they start very early) The housing crisis is still on in Ireland so it can be quite difficult to find good accommodation that is reasonably priced. I got lucky and had a 24/7 bus that would take me straight from campus and home, and in the evening the bus drive was only 40 minutes from the city center. I would therefore encourage people to get a head start as soon as you know you want to go to Dublin, and start to search for accommodation sooner rather than later.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you find a place where the public transport options are good, as it can be a bit tricky otherwise. Especially if you count on staying out late as not all busses have 24-hour service.

questions.answer:
We could contact our erasmus coordinator on mail, visit them in person if we had arrived or there was also a chatbot ish thing on
my.tcd.ie
that you could ask directly. I never used it though as the registration process was fairly straightforward.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, which I had to fill out in a Google questionaire made for that specific purpose. It seems that at least the law schools process for registrering classes is very transparent and easy to manage.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Advice isn't really needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some really good teachers and the courses I took were very interesting and at the same time weren't that challenging so I felt I had the time to comfortably make experiences outside of the classroom as well which was nice.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say the courses that I took (International Human Rights Law, Equality Law and Refugee Law) when comparing to the courses I have so far had at UCPH were slightly "easier" level wise. Trinity had a very good academic programme and I did feel that the level was high at certain times, but I would say that all in all I could relax more during my courses than I would be able to back home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I prefered the style of teaching at Trinity as the teachers were more laidback in a sense, while at the same time being able to be a bit more inspiring when talking in their respective fields. They also went out of their way to incorporate and invite relevant people to have a chat during seminars with the students were we could go more in depth with the subject and engage with it in more than in just a theoretical sense.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Human Rights Law, Equality Law and Refugee Law.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Der var nærmest et society for ALT hvad man kan tænke sig til, lige fra film, strikkeklub, circus society, diverse sportsgrene, musik, revy osv. Det virkede til at der oprigtigt er noget for alle.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Jeg kastede mig ud i Touch Rugby hvilket var en virkelig fed oplevelse. Det er en mindre agressiv version af klassisk rugby og en god måde at få lidt motion og et fællesskab på - og så var det også mere af en social sport så selvom vi trænede teknikker og spillede kampe var det ikke alt for seriøst og der var altid et socialt arrangement efter. Derudover kan jeg anbefale circus society som var lidt syret (jeg prøvede at lære at cykle på en-hjulet, men det lykkedes aldrig...) og film society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: PUBS. Der er ikke så overraskende en kæmpe pub kultur i Dublin og i sær dem der ligger lige ved campus er yndet besøg af studerende. Live music på en klassisk irsk pub kan noget helt magisk, og man behøver heldigvis heller ikke at drikke Guinness for at nyde det. Jeg tog tid ud af kalenderen til at rejse lidt rundt efter endt undervisning og det kan jeg også kun kraftigt anbefale. Irland er egentlig ikke så stor en ø så man kan nå en masse. Et par weekendudflugter undervejs i semesteret vil jeg også anbefale, eksempelvis en dags tur til Howth eller Bray som kun ligger 40-ish minutter fra Dublin i tog, men leder til fantastiske vandremuligheder.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Meget nemt. Jeg faldt i fælden med at primært omgås andre udvekslingsstuderende hvilket ikke er så underligt da det er netop det miljø man dumper ned i. Det lykkedes dog også i gennem at være aktiv i diverse foreninger og generelt at være åben, at møde nogle lokale irer som jeg i dag betragter som gode venner.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nej, jeg var selv rigtig elendig til at falde i snak om i hvert fald de studerende jeg havde undervisning med. Det var meget at dukke op til forelæsning, sidde der og så tage væk igen. Der hvor jeg fik interageret med de lokale studerende var helt klart mest i de forskellige societies jeg deltog i, så jeg vil helt klart anbefale at melde sig ind i 2-4 man synes rammer ens interesser eller bare lyder spændende.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Afslappetheden, det var meget nemt at snakke med folk og folk tog sjældent dem selv så seriøst hvilket var dejligt. Dublin og craic går hånd i hånd.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing asap, socialize from day 1 and while you should take your courses seriously don't drown in coursework and remember to enjoy your experience besides the studying part.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Undgå Temple Bar området, det er dyrt for absolut ingen grund.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Uden tvivl de mennesker jeg mødte, og som jeg allerede har planer om at besøge så snart min bankkonto er kommet sig ovenpå første tur. Dublin er virkelig en fantastisk by, med en masse fantastiske mennesker og man keder sig aldrig da der altid sker noget, selv om søndagen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Funding was a little tight at times haha, but I managed.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
